      "text": "The command `del` only deletes files, not folders, and `Windows.old` is a special system folder protected by high-level permissions (TrustedInstaller).\n\nHere are the three ways to delete it, ranked from easiest to most forceful.\n\n### Method 1: Disk Cleanup (The Correct Way)\nThis is the safest method because Windows handles the permissions for you.\n\n1.  Press the **Start** button and type **Disk Cleanup**.\n2.  Right-click the result and choose **Run as administrator**.\n3.  Select your **C:** drive and click OK.\n4.  **Crucial Step:** Click the button labeled **Clean up system files** (bottom left).\n5.  Wait for it to scan again.\n6.  Scroll down the list and check the box for **Previous Windows installation(s)**.\n7.  Click **OK** and then **Delete Files**.\n\n---\n\n### Method 2: Storage Settings (The Modern Way)\nIf you are on Windows 10 or 11, you can use the Settings menu.\n\n1.  Go to **Settings** \u003e **System** \u003e **Storage**.\n2.  Click on **Temporary files**.\n3.  Wait for the scan to finish.\n4.  Check the box for **Previous Windows installation(s)**.\n5.  Click **Remove files**.\n\n---\n\n### Method 3: Command Prompt (The \"Force\" Way)\nIf you prefer the command line, `del` won\u0027t work. You must use `rd` (remove directory) and you usually need to take ownership of the folder first.\n\n**Run Command Prompt as Administrator** and enter these commands one by one:\n\n1.  **Take ownership of the folder:**\n    ```cmd\n    takeown /F C:\\Windows.old /A /R /D Y\n    ```\n    *(This may take a minute as it scrolls through all files)*\n\n2.  **Grant full permission to Administrators:**\n    ```cmd\n    icacls C:\\Windows.old /grant *S-1-5-32-544:F /T /C /Q\n    ```\n\n3.  **Delete the folder:**\n    ```cmd\n    rd /s /q C:\\Windows.old\n    ```\n\n*Note: If `rd` still gives you an error, reboot your computer and try the command again; sometimes a file inside the folder is locked by a running process.*",
